findings.text: Registration entry accepts a console descriptor and makes it visible for printing after validation and enablement. It rejects duplicate registration, refuses late boot consoles when a real console exists, prepares nonblocking resources, resolves enablement through preferred and default selection, assigns an initial sequence, inserts the descriptor into the global list with preferred head handling, announces enablement, retires boot consoles when a preferred real console takes over unless retention is requested, and reconciles printer threads before releasing the list guard.

Console list lock, unlock and held assertion are service interfaces for serializing list changes. Lock provides exclusive entry, unlock releases it, and the assertion lets callees verify the caller holds the guard before touching list state or starting and stopping printer threads.

Nonblocking console resource management offers allocation, release and printer thread stop. Allocation validates required callbacks, initializes wait and deferred work state, presets sequence tracking to a maximal value pending explicit forcing, and provides printing buffers with shared buffers for boot consoles and private buffers plus optional thread creation for others. Release synchronizes deferred work, stops threads, clears state and frees private buffers. Stop is idempotent when no thread exists. A fallback configuration provides nonfunctional allocation and release.

Enablement resolves in order from user specified preferred entries to platform preferred entries to already enabled descriptors. Matching uses driver matching when present otherwise name and index comparison with index adoption when unspecified. Setup runs under boot synchronization and failure aborts enablement. Success marks enabled and marks preferred device when the entry is the chosen console. Default enablement applies when no preferred console exists and the list is empty or the head lacks a device or is a boot console, adopting a zero index, running setup without options, and marking preferred device when a device is bound. Braille flagged consoles do not proceed to normal printing.

List ordering keeps the preferred device at the head. An empty list makes the newcomer head with preferred marking. A newcomer already marked preferred displaces the prior head marking and becomes head. Others insert behind the head. Removal clears enabled state, unlinks with deferred reclamation, transfers preferred marking to the new head when needed, waits for readers, recomputes global presence flags for boot, legacy and nonblocking types, releases nonblocking resources, notifies listeners, runs exit handling and reconciles printer threads.

Initial sequence depends on replay and boot marking. Consoles requesting replay or flagged boot start from a consistent copy of the syslog sequence taken under its guard. Others start from the next ring sequence, with a boot handover path that flushes all consoles under the printing guard and otherwise falls back to the lowest sequence among enabled boot consoles, reading nonblocking and legacy progress accordingly. Handover to a preferred real console while boot consoles exist suppresses replay to avoid duplicate output on the same device. Nonblocking consoles receive the start through forcing while legacy consoles store it directly.

Console list mutation requires holding the list mutex from lock to unlock. Entry warns when attempted inside SRCU read side. Allocation, release, thread creation and stop, legacy thread creation and thread reconciliation all assert the guard is held. Registration holds it across validation, selection, insertion, announcement, boot retirement and reconciliation. Unregistration holds it across announcement, unlink, reader wait, flag recomputation, release and reconciliation.

Hardware transition for atomic capable nonblocking consoles is guarded by driver device callbacks around list insertion and removal. Console setup and boot handover flushing run under the printing guard to serialize against boot output and to allow safe progress reads. Syslog sequence copy runs under the syslog guard. Removal uses an SRCU wait after unlink so later cleanup and exit handling are invisible to readers.

Printer thread orchestration has an inactive configuration that does nothing and an active configuration that manages legacy and nonblocking workers. The legacy worker exists when legacy or boot consoles are present and forced operation requests it, with creation failure causing removal of all blocking consoles, and it stops when neither type remains. Nonblocking workers start only after readiness, with no boot console present and at least one nonblocking console present, creating one worker per nonblocking console and removing consoles whose worker fails to start. A running flag tracks whether nonblocking workers should exist and is cleared when boot consoles return or the last nonblocking console leaves.

Observed console descriptor carries identity, flags, sequence state, callbacks and runtime linkage as used by registration and printing. Identity includes name, index and list linkage. Flags distinguish boot, enabled, preferred device, nonblocking, replay and Braille. Sequence state includes legacy progress and nonblocking progress with previous progress and atomic state. Callbacks include matching, setup, exit, device guarding and threaded plus atomic output. Runtime includes printing buffers, printer thread, deferred work, wait object and drop count. Full layout with offsets and sizes is not shown.

Debug entry points include a SysRQ handler that reports missing IO support, announces pending connection when unconnected, then raises a breakpoint, together with descriptor labels for help and action. A reboot notifier selects among entering the debugger, detaching the remote stub or doing nothing based on reboot mode. Stub exit reports status to the peer and flushes output when connected with IO support outside KDB mode, then marks disconnected.

Late debug initialization clears early mode, invokes an architecture hook when IO is registered, completes KDB initialization, and optionally blocks waiting for a remote peer when an early break was requested. KDB initialization is level gated and runs once, building the main command table and breakpoint table at the first level and executing startup commands with forced closure of an incomplete macro at the later level. Breakpoint table setup clears storage, marks all slots free and registers breakpoint commands plus a hardware command when the platform advertises hardware breakpoint support. Table registration appends entries to a global command list.

Failure handling warns and ignores duplicate registration, refuses late boot registration, fails allocation on missing threaded or device callbacks, and aborts registration with resource cleanup on buffer, thread or enablement failure including Braille exclusion. Legacy worker creation failure removes all blocking consoles while per console nonblocking worker failure removes that console. Concurrent hardware use during transition to registered state is contained with the device guard. Boot log visibility loss on retirement is mitigated by announcing enablement on all consoles before removing boot consoles.

Maximal sequence for unsigned long representation has two configurations. One is a fixed all bits set value. The other derives from the first ring sequence plus one half of the thirty two bit range through a sixty four to unsigned long sequence conversion. The next sequence helper in this configuration is a constant placeholder. Exact widths and conversion details depend on unrouted definitions.

Console status reporting prefixes messages to distinguish blocking versus nonblocking operation and boot versus regular consoles alongside identity. It is used for enablement and disablement announcements and for reporting buffer allocation and thread creation failures.

Braille handling routes flagged consoles to dedicated registration paths. When command line options carry Braille settings the descriptor is flagged and passed to Braille registration. Unregistration delegates flagged consoles to Braille release first, aborting on error and short circuiting on positive return. Fallback configurations report success without action.
